title: Personal Sender Account KYC Refresh Interval After an Upgrade
content:
The refresh interval of an upgraded Personal Sender Account — the time from the upgrade to its next periodic identity (KYC) review — is a whole number of calendar months.

- **Standard refresh interval.** The standard refresh interval is 36 calendar months counted from the upgrade date, the periodic review interval of Paloma Verified and Paloma Verified Plus, the levels an agent applies.
- **Risk-weighted refresh interval.** The risk-weighted refresh interval starts from the standard refresh interval and is never below 12 months.
- **Refresh interval.** The refresh interval is the risk-weighted refresh interval, and never fewer than 3 months.
- **Due date.** The next periodic review of an upgraded account falls due the refresh interval, in whole calendar months, after the upgrade date, on the same day of the month or on the last day of a shorter month.

## Worked example (hypothetical dates)

An account is moved up to Paloma Verified Plus on 30 November of a given year. With a refresh interval of 36 months, the next periodic review falls due on 30 November three years later.

| Upgrade date | Refresh interval (months) | Next periodic review due |
|---|---|---|
| 30 November | 36 | 30 November, three years later |
| 31 May | 36 | 31 May, three years later |
| 29 February (leap year) | 36 | 28 February, three years later (the last day of that shorter month) |

The day of the month is kept; where the month reached is too short for it, the last day of that month is used.
